instruction:
Use Godot stable documentation to review a game that has a menu over its gameplay view. Read Using InputEvent, Input examples, and Mouse and input coordinates. Explain the relative order of _input, GUI input and _unhandled_input, and identify the documented methods used to mark events handled. Compare event callbacks with polling for a single jump press versus movement while a key is held, and explain the advantage of named Input Map actions over hard-coded keys. Finally distinguish event.position from event.relative when the mouse is captured and identify the documented way to get the viewport size. Give a compact recommendation for the menu/gameplay case, cite all three pages, and record the displayed stable documentation version if available. Research documentation only; do not open an editor, execute code or modify a project.

Stopping condition: Stop when the routing order, handling methods, event/polling and Input Map comparisons, captured-mouse distinction and viewport-size reference are reported with three source-page citations.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.description: Explains the relative order of _input, GUI input, and _unhandled_input based on the documentation. Full credit for stating the correct sequence.

items.criterion: Identify methods to mark events handled
items.description: Identifies the documented methods used to mark events as handled in the input and GUI paths, according to the cited documentation. Full credit when the applicable methods are correctly identified; do not treat a single illustrative method as the complete requirement.
Compares event callbacks with polling for a single jump press versus movement while a key is held, accurately reflecting the documentation's examples.
Explains the advantage of named Input Map actions over hard-coded keys as described in the documentation (e.g., decoupling physical keys from actions, supporting multiple keys/controllers).
Distinguishes between event.position and event.relative when the mouse is captured, based on the 'Mouse and input coordinates' page.

items.criterion: Identify method to get viewport size
items.description: Identifies the documented way to get the viewport size (e.g., `get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size` or `get_viewport_rect().size`).
Gives a compact recommendation for handling inputs in the menu/gameplay case (e.g., GUI handling the menu and consuming the event so gameplay's _unhandled_input doesn't trigger).
Explicitly cites all three required pages: 'Using InputEvent', 'Input examples', and 'Mouse and input coordinates'.
Records the displayed stable documentation version if available (e.g., Godot 4.x stable). Full credit if recorded, or if reported as unavailable despite checking.
